content.text: Updated: Mar. 17, 2026, 12:31 p.m.Published: Mar. 17, 2026, 12:30 p.m.Glimt's players celebrate at the end of the Champions League playoff soccer match between Inter Milan and Bodo Glimt, at the San Siro stadium in Milan, Italy, Tuesday, Feb.24, 2026. (AP Photo/Luca Bruno)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.Sporting CP faces Bodø/Glimt in the UEFA Champions League Round of 16 second leg on Tuesday, March 17, at Estádio José Alvalade in Libson, Portugal.Fans can watch the match on CBS Sports Network for free with a trial of FuboTV. You can also watch the match on Paramount Plus, the exclusive English-language home of the Champions League in the U.S.The CBS streaming service’s deal with the Champions League carries through the 2029-30 season, including the knockout stage, final and the UEFA Europa League.Here’s what you need to know:Date: Tuesday, March 17, 2026Time: 1:45 p.m. ETLocation: Estádio José AlvaladeStreaming/TV: CBS Sports Network, Paramount+***Here’s a soccer story via the Associated Press:Protecting three-goal leads, Champions League heavyweights Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain will look to clinch their places in the quarterfinals on Tuesday. So, amazingly, will tiny Bodø/Glimt.There’s a one-sided look to the first batch of second-leg matches to be completed in the round of 16, as Madrid and PSG arrive in England with a 3-0 lead over Manchester City and a 5-2 lead over Chelsea, respectively.This could be a tough week for the much-hyped Premier League, as all six of its round-of-16 representatives failed to win across the first legs.Arsenal looks best placed of the English teams to advance and will take on Bayer Leverkusen in London on Tuesday with the score at 1-1.Then there’s Bodø/Glimt, in its debut season in the Champions League and easily the least-heralded team to make it through to the knockout stage.The Norwegian club leads Sporting Lisbon 3-0 from the first leg and is looking to complete another upset, having eliminated Inter Milan — last season’s runner-up — in the playoff round and beaten Man City and Atletico Madrid in its final two matches of the first phase to avoid getting knocked out.No Norwegian club has reached the quarterfinals since Rosenborg in 1997.Calling all soccer fans!
